key_insight: Cluster-based Sequential Feature Selection (CSFS) uses clustering to make wrapper-based feature selection more efficient while preserving prediction quality for renewable energy forecasting.
engineering_relevance: For wind and solar power prediction pipelines, CSFS can reduce feature-selection compute cost and simplify model inputs without sacrificing accuracy.
method: Cluster input variables into groups before sequential wrapper selection.
Compare CSFS against SFS, filter methods, and Random Forest feature importance.
Use a model-agnostic workflow that is designed for reproducible feature selection.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluated CSFS on real-world wind turbine power curve modeling and photovoltaic power prediction and found performance comparable to SFS with an average 21% lower computational cost.
watch_item: Results depend on the specific datasets and feature sets studied, so the clustering strategy and wrapper settings may need retuning for other renewable-energy sites or sensors.
paper_title: Improving Wind and Solar Power Prediction with Efficient Wrapper-based Feature Selection: An Empirical Study
